A.explanation: This is $\Delta L / F = 0.40/2.4 \approx 0.17 \text{ m N}^{-1}$, the inverse of the spring constant.

B.explanation: This is final length divided by force, $0.60/2.4 = 0.25 \text{ m N}^{-1}$, which uses length instead of extension.

C.explanation: This is $F / L = 2.4/0.60 = 4.0 \text{ N m}^{-1}$, which incorrectly uses total length $0.60 \text{ m}$ instead of extension.

D.explanation: Force $2.4 \text{ N}$ produces extension $0.40 \text{ m}$, so $k = 2.4/0.40 = 6.0 \text{ N m}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice the graph plots length in $\text{m}$ against force in $\text{N}$, and it starts at $0.20 \text{ m}$ when $F = 0$ - that intercept is the unstretched length.
Recall Hooke's law $F = k x$ uses extension $x$, not total length, so you must subtract the $0.20 \text{ m}$ starting length from the $0.60 \text{ m}$ final length.
Calculate the extension for $F = 2.4 \text{ N}$ and then use $k = F/x$ to find $k$ in $\text{N m}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Read the intercept on the length axis: at $F = 0$, length $L_0 = 0.20 \text{ m}$. This is the natural length of the spring.
Read the final point: at $F = 2.4 \text{ N}$, length $L = 0.60 \text{ m}$.
Hooke's law is $F = kx$, where $x$ is extension. Calculate extension as change in length: $x = L - L_0 = 0.60 - 0.20 = 0.40 \text{ m}$.
Substitute values with units: $k = 2.4/0.40 = 6.0 \text{ N m}^{-1}$. The unit check gives $\text{N m}^{-1}$ as required. This is option D.
